target_profile.system_boundary: Captured Go raft library: main role loop, per-peer replication and heartbeats, FSM and snapshot workers, injectable transports/stores/FSM. No production deployment or caller application is supplied.
protocol_contexts: Per-leader commitment object and worker generation
external_interfaces: Transport RPC and optional heartbeat fast path
LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and caller FSM
ownership: Main loop owns leader state and configuration
Independent workers send support through locked commitment and verification objects
Network fast-path may process empty heartbeats concurrently with blocking main RPC
selection_injection: NewRaft takes caller-supplied stores, transport, FSM and validated Config; in-repository implementations are not assumed externalized
unknowns: Full production persistence, transport failure semantics and application-specific FSM contracts remain outside this initial trace

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement
activities.realization_summary: Per-session voter matches produce monotone commitment after current-term startIndex; followers use accepted leader commit indications.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
activities.realization_summary: Pre-vote and persisted voting establish a local leader role; RPCs, response signals, lease checks, removal and transfer change it. Verification is a separate authority observation path.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
activities.realization_summary: Constructor rebuilds term, history and membership; snapshot install restores FSM before reply; manual restore is explicitly exceptional.
Latest/committed log configurations select voting and commitment membership while replication includes nonvoters.
Dedicated FSM worker consumes committed batches and returns application responses; dispatch progress is not completion.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
activities.realization_summary: LogStore and StableStore support retained logs and terms/votes; snapshot worker persists applied state. In-repository InmemStore is test-only; other backend semantics remain open.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion
activities.realization_summary: Apply admission is a future, not completion; nonleader, shutdown, enqueue and leadership-loss cases differ. VerifyLeader promises leadership assurance.

surfaces.reason: Heartbeat refreshes contact even on unsuccessful replies and lacks the ordinary replication response-term check. Need permitted blocked-progress schedule and precise lease contract before drawing a consequence.
Separate term/candidate writes and duplicate-vote reuse invite partial-write recovery analysis; concrete backend/fault responsibility not established.

surfaces.entry_point: NetworkTransport heartbeat callback concurrent with appendEntries/installSnapshot
surfaces.reason: Actual fast-path ownership differs from main-thread comments. Need same-history ordering, durable update semantics and real transport schedules.
Manual recovery is separately documented at the API boundary; its full implementation and backend failure variants have not been expanded in this normal-operation map.

core_overview.rationale: Representative normal command formation and authority acquisition/loss have been followed through real producers, consumers, membership, storage, recovery and completion. Usable identifies a sourced investigation basis, not verified correctness or exhaustive coverage.

formation.explanation: Apply creates a future on applyCh. The leader main loop assigns index/term and stores logs; only successful storage reports local match. Per-peer workers send real AppendEntries with previous-log identity, term and leader commit index. Receiver rejects stale terms or mismatched prefix, truncates conflicts, stores new suffix and updates configuration before successful response. Successful nonempty append or snapshot installation advances that worker's captured session commitment. Commitment counts only current voter IDs and requires a majority match reaching the first index of this tenure; leaderLoop consumes commitCh, records commitment and queues committed entries. Followers learn commit index from ordinary replication; empty independent heartbeat carries neither entries nor commit index. processLogs dispatches in order to runFSM; command completion follows Apply/ApplyBatch return, while the main-loop lastApplied value only tracks dispatch. Replication retry and snapshot fallback recover lagging peers.

context.explanation: Startup reads durable term and log, restores snapshot/FSM and membership, replays suffix configurations and starts as Follower. Ordinary contact timeout campaigns only for a local voter. Optional pre-vote does not persist a vote; actual electSelf increments durable term, persists self-vote and sends one request per voter into a campaign-specific channel. RequestVote rejects stale history/term, disallowed membership or another known leader (transfer excepted), and persists vote before grant. Candidate majority enters Leader; newer term responses, received append, lease quorum loss or committed local removal exit it. Leadership transfer first catches the target up, suppresses new leader work, then sends TimeoutNow to trigger election without pre-vote. VerifyLeader separately registers an authority observation with replication workers and returns from aggregate support; that support eligibility is an open local question.

connection.explanation: Every tenure creates a new commitment object, isolated replication workers and an initial term no-op. Existing durable history survives role loss, but old worker replies retain the old commitment/channel and do not certify a new tenure. Current-term commitment reconciles inherited history before allowing a new membership change. Membership activates latest voter eligibility at configuration append; retained voter matches survive by permanent ServerID, while new voters start at zero. Only one uncommitted configuration is admitted and committed local removal ends leadership. Exit fails pending inflight/verify futures, while already committed work queued to the FSM continues; ErrLeadershipLost is explicitly ambiguous about actual commitment. Recovery restores snapshot index/term/configuration and reconstructs latest configuration from retained logs. Snapshot production pairs applied state with committed configuration; manual Restore is an explicitly exceptional recovery operation that aborts inflight work and forces snapshot propagation followed by no-op commitment. Verification support differs from log support: all replication workers can notify pending verification, although voter filtering protects log commitment and lease quorum. This distinction supplies a focused question rather than a conclusion about safety.
